name: Warsong Scout Update
summary: Orders from Kadrak reach Warsong Scout Update as scouts watch the contested woods. The Horde depends on their reports to guard its positions in Ashenvale against night elf attacks.

sections.title: Eyes in the Shadows
sections.body: Kadrak depends on scattered Warsong scouts to watch the Ashenvale border. The forest gives night elf sentinels cover, and the scouts face the risk of being cut off. Couriers carry written updates between them so isolated outposts can report what they see and remain connected to Horde command.

sections.title: Holding the Ground
sections.body: Warsong scouts watch for night elf raids meant to reclaim the forest. Every stretch of Ashenvale the clan has cleared or occupied has cost lives. Kadrak's orders keep the forward scouts in touch with the Horde and give them a way to report that their defenses are holding against elven resistance.

faq.answer: Kadrak is a Horde commander on the boundary between the Barrens and Ashenvale. He coordinates scouting, border defense, and supplies for Warsong operations in the forest.

faq.q: Why are the Warsong scouts so paranoid about night elves?
faq.answer: Night elves know how to hide in their ancestral forests and strike Horde patrols by surprise. The Warsong Clan clears lumber and settles land the elves consider sacred, leaving its scouts at risk of sudden attack.

faq.q: Why is Ashenvale being fought over?
faq.answer: The Horde needs Ashenvale's lumber and other resources to build Orgrimmar and supply settlements in the Barrens and Durotar. The night elves consider the forest sacred and fight to drive out the orcish loggers and garrisons.

faq.q: What is the Warsong Clan's role here?
faq.answer: The Warsong Clan leads the Horde's effort to claim resources in Ashenvale. Grom Hellscream led them into the woods during the Third War. They remain entrenched there, operating lumber camps and fighting the Sentinels.

faq.q: Where does this report go after reaching the scout?
faq.answer: After receiving Kadrak's instructions, the scout reports local success against elven counterattacks. The report keeps Horde leaders informed about conditions at the front.

faq.q: Are the Horde's plans in Ashenvale succeeding at this point?
faq.answer: The frontline scouts believe their defenses are holding: they keep their fortified positions and fend off elven attacks. Ashenvale remains fiercely contested, with neither side in full control.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you help keep its Ashenvale foothold secure when you carry orders from Kadrak to the outer scouts, who face night elf ambushes.
As an orc, you inherit the Warsong Clan's fight for timber in Ashenvale, where the land and its ancient defenders resist them.
As a night elf, you see Warsong scouts on the borders as a continuing desecration of Elune's sacred forests, which the Sentinels strive to purge.
